message.text: Searching the codebase for all distinct server surfaces that enforce memo visibility. At least three enforcement sites exist.
I'll search the server for every place memo visibility is enforced.

The focus is on distinct HTTP and RPC surfaces that enforce memo visibility, not helper functions.

API v1 endpoints, RSS feeds, fileserver attachments, SSE hub, email notifications, and share links are being evaluated as distinct enforcement sites.

gRPC/Connect API memo service, attachment API, and share service are now under review. The distinction between true enforcement and simple visibility propagation is being checked against key files.

Checking GetMemoByShare, ACL/authorizer, MCP, and attachment service as distinct enforcement surfaces. Beginning to list the main sites.

Enumerating potential enforcement sites across the API v1 memo read and list paths, RSS, frontend sitemap, file server, SSE hub, email notifications, share logic, attachment API, and per-handler checks. The focus is on distinct HTTP entry points rather than individual helper functions.

GetMemoByShare bypasses visibility checks via share tokens. It does not enforce memo visibility, so it is excluded from the list.

I am organizing distinct enforcement sites by server surface. These include the API memo read helper, list and query filters, attachment access, HTTP file server permissions, RSS, frontend sitemap, and SSE delivery.

Email notifications, in-app notifications, and per-RPC checks for comments, reactions, attachments, and mentions are additional enforcement sites. The response will list the six distinct HTTP and RPC entry surfaces.

The nine enforcement sites are mapped to specific files: `checkMemoReadAccess` in `memo_service.go`, `ListMemos` visibility filter in `memo_service.go`, `checkAttachmentPermission` in `fileserver.go`, RSS `VisibilityList: Public` in `rss.go`, frontend sitemap in `frontend.go`, SSE `canReceive` in `sse_hub.go`, email `canViewerAccessMemo` in `notification/email.go`, attachment API in `attachment_service.go`, and inbox notifications in `user_service_notifications.go`. These may collapse into six distinct server surfaces: API, RSS, file server, frontend, SSE, and email.

The final list now names seven distinct enforcement sites. API v1 memo read access and list filters are in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`. HTTP file server attachment access is in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`. RSS feeds are in `server/router/rss/rss.go`. The frontend sitemap is in `server/router/frontend/frontend.go`. SSE delivery is in `server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`. Email notifications are in `server/notification/email.go`.

Reaction, comment, and memo attachment services each duplicate memo visibility checks instead of delegating to `checkMemoReadAccess`. These are separate enforcement sites. The final list now includes eight distinct surfaces.

The final list now names ten distinct enforcement sites. API read checks, list and query filters, attachment access, file server permissions, RSS, frontend sitemap, SSE delivery, email notifications, inbox notifications, and inline checks for comments, reactions, and mentions are all listed separately.

The list is being trimmed to eight distinct enforcement surfaces. Share tokens are excluded as a bypass mechanism, not an enforcement site. Each remaining surface independently controls memo visibility.

h15.
`checkMemoReadAccess` (GetMemo / parent reads) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`  
`ListMemos` / related query filters — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` (also `user_service_stats.go`, `memo_relation_service.go`, `memo_service_converter.go`)  
HTTP file-server attachment access — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`  
RSS feeds (public only) — `server/router/rss/rss.go`  
Sitemap (public only) — `server/router/frontend/frontend.go`  
SSE delivery (`SSEClient.canReceive`) — `server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`  
Attachment RPC access — `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go`  
Notification email (`canViewerAccessMemo`) — `server/notification/email.go`  
Inbox notification filtering — `server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go`

ACL only marks memo RPCs public and leaves visibility to the service (`server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go`). The same PRIVATE/PUBLIC/PROTECTED rules are copied on comments, reactions, memo attachments, and mentions (`memo_service_comments.go`, `reaction_service.go`, `memo_attachment_service.go`, `memo_mention_helpers.go`). `GetMemoByShare` does not apply visibility; the share token is the access check.
